description: Issue-tracker / standup assistant with issue search, due-date listing, sprint info, and issue lookup tools.

tools.name: search_issues
tools.description: Search issues in the tracker. Returns issues whose last-update timestamp falls in [updated_after, updated_before). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); updated_after is inclusive, updated_before is exclusive.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text filter on issue name (optional; empty returns all issues in range)

params.name: status
params.description: Status filter, e.g. open, in_progress, in_review, done (optional)

params.name: updated_after
params.description: Range start on last-update time, UTC ISO 8601, inclusive

params.name: updated_before
params.description: Range end on last-update time, UTC ISO 8601, exclusive

tools.name: list_due
tools.description: List issues by due date. Returns issues whose due timestamp falls in [due_after, due_before). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); due_after is inclusive, due_before is exclusive.

params.name: due_after
params.description: Range start on due time, UTC ISO 8601, inclusive

params.name: due_before
params.description: Range end on due time, UTC ISO 8601, exclusive

tools.name: get_sprint
tools.description: Return the current sprint: name, start and end timestamps (UTC ISO 8601).

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: Look up a single issue by its ID (e.g. PM-207). Returns the issue record including its last-update timestamp.

scenarios.title: due-by-end-of-next-week
scenarios.user: What's due by the end of next week?

verifyPhrase.phrase: by the end of next week
verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time resolves 'end of next week' as the closing stretch of next week ([2026-07-29T04:00Z .. 2026-08-02T04:00Z)), but a 'due by' deadline question means [now .. end-of-next-week). The bridge's END instant 2026-08-02T04:00:00Z agrees with the Sunday-start end golden; only the start-side semantics differ.

checks.note: PM-311, PM-318, PM-322 are due before every admissible end; PM-330 (Aug 4) and the already-past PM-301 (Jul 20) are not

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 22 2026, 9:10am EDT (UTC-4) — midweek so both week conventions agree on next week's interior. 'By the end of next week' = [start, end-of-next-week). End: Sunday-start (en-US CLDR) next week is Sun Jul 26..Sat Aug 1, so end = Sun Aug 2 00:00 ET = 2026-08-02T04:00Z (this matches the bridge's END for 'end of next week'); Monday-start (ISO) next week is Mon Jul 27..Sun Aug 2, end = Mon Aug 3 00:00 ET = 2026-08-03T04:00Z. Start: now itself (2026-07-22T13:10Z) or start of today (Jul 22 00:00 ET = 04:00Z); both admitted, crossed with both ends = 4 tuples. Rows: PM-311 Thu Jul 23 3pm ET, PM-318 Tue Jul 28 noon ET, and PM-322 at 2026-08-01T02:00Z = Fri Jul 31 10:00pm EDT (UTC-day Aug 1 flavor row) are inside ALL tuples; PM-330 Tue Aug 4 is past both ends; PM-301 Mon Jul 20 predates both starts. No rows between today-start and now, and none on the disputed edge day Sun Aug 2 local, so the count is 3 under every tuple.

scenarios.title: standup-shipped-yesterday
scenarios.user: Standup time — what did the team ship yesterday?

checks.note: Dark mode toggle (Mon 2pm CDT) and Export to CSV (Mon 10:30pm CDT)
Must include the late-Monday-evening ship and exclude the Sunday-night one

scenarios.rationale: Now = TUESDAY Jul 28 2026, 8:45am CDT (UTC-5). Yesterday = civil Monday Jul 27 in Chicago: [Jul 27 00:00 CT, Jul 28 00:00 CT) = [2026-07-27T05:00Z, 2026-07-28T05:00Z). Double UTC trap: PM-407 (2026-07-28T03:30Z) is Monday 10:30pm CDT — inside — while PM-398 (2026-07-27T04:15Z) is Sunday 11:15pm CDT — outside — yet naive UTC-day bounds [Jul 27 00Z, Jul 28 00Z) select exactly the wrong one of the pair. PM-402 (Mon 2:00pm CDT) is interior; PM-395 (Fri Jul 24) is out of range. Correct: 2 issues shipped — PM-402 and PM-407.

scenarios.title: touched-past-24-hours
scenarios.user: Which issues were touched in the past 24 hours?

checks.note: PM-511, PM-509, PM-514; PM-502 was updated 25h40m before now

scenarios.rationale: Now = SATURDAY Aug 1 2026, 5:40pm EDT (UTC-4), i.e. 2026-08-01T21:40Z — window sits on the Jul/Aug month boundary. 'Past 24 hours' is pure hour arithmetic, not a civil day: [now-24h, now) = [2026-07-31T21:40Z, 2026-08-01T21:40Z), matching the bridge exactly. In range: PM-511 (Jul 31 22:30Z = Fri 6:30pm EDT, 50 min after the start), PM-509 (Aug 1 02:30Z = Fri 10:30pm EDT), PM-514 (Aug 1 15:00Z = Sat 11:00am EDT) — count 3. PM-502 (Jul 31 20:00Z) is 25h40m before now — excluded; an agent that rounds to 'since midnight' or 'since yesterday 00:00' would wrongly include it (its bounds also fail arg grading).

scenarios.title: sprint-end-local-day
scenarios.user: When does the current sprint end?

checks.note: Sprint ends 11:59pm EDT July 31; the UTC timestamp reads August 1 — must answer July 31
If a time is given it must be 11:59 pm local, not 3:59

scenarios.rationale: Pure time→NL: get_sprint takes no arguments and returns end_utc = 2026-08-01T03:59:00Z. In America/New_York (EDT, UTC-4) that is FRIDAY July 31 2026, 11:59pm — the classic end-of-day sprint boundary stored in UTC. Correct answers say the sprint ends Friday July 31; 'August 1' is the naive UTC-day reading and fails (rejectUtcDay — days verified to differ). clockTime fires only if a clock time appears, in which case it must be the local 11:59 pm, not 03:59 (clocks verified to differ).

scenarios.title: still-open-from-june

checks.note: PM-233, PM-241, and PM-248 (last touched Jun 30 10:30pm EDT); PM-229 was May 31 local and PM-252 is July

scenarios.rationale: Now = SUNDAY Jul 19 2026, 6:00pm EDT. 'From June' = the June 2026 civil month in the user's zone: Jun 1 00:00 ET..Jul 1 00:00 ET = [2026-06-01T04:00Z, 2026-07-01T04:00Z) (EDT, UTC-4, throughout). Symmetric UTC trap at both edges: PM-248 (2026-07-01T02:30Z) is Jun 30 10:30pm EDT — inside local June though its UTC day is July 1 — while PM-229 (2026-06-01T03:00Z) is May 31 11:00pm EDT — outside local June though its UTC day is June 1. Naive UTC-month bounds [Jun 1 00Z, Jul 1 00Z) swap exactly those two rows. PM-252 (Jul 10) is out of range. All in-range rows have status open, so the count is 3 regardless of status filtering.

scenarios.title: changed-while-out-last-week
scenarios.user: I was out last week — what changed while I was gone?

checks.note: PM-152, PM-160, PM-166 under either week convention; PM-170 is this week, PM-149 the week before

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 8 2026, 11:30am EDT — midweek on purpose so both week conventions agree on the interior; last week straddles the Jun/Jul month boundary. Sunday-start (en-US CLDR): Sun Jun 28..Sun Jul 5 = [2026-06-28T04:00Z, 2026-07-05T04:00Z) (matches the bridge); Monday-start (ISO): Mon Jun 29..Mon Jul 6 = [2026-06-29T04:00Z, 2026-07-06T04:00Z). In range under BOTH: PM-152 Tue Jun 30 11:00am ET, PM-160 Thu Jul 2 2:20pm ET, and PM-166 at 2026-07-05T02:10Z = SATURDAY Jul 4 10:10pm EDT — the trap row, whose UTC day (Jul 5) would fall outside a naive UTC Sunday-start window [Jun 28 00Z, Jul 5 00Z). PM-170 (Tue Jul 7, this week) and PM-149 (Fri Jun 26, the week before) are outside both readings. No rows on the disputed edge days (Sun Jun 28, Sun Jul 5 local), so the count is 3 under every admissible tuple.

scenarios.title: berlin-due-tomorrow

checks.note: Must include the just-after-midnight Friday ticket and exclude the just-after-midnight Saturday one

scenarios.rationale: Now = THURSDAY Jul 16 2026, 3:20pm CEST (Berlin summer time, UTC+2). Tomorrow = civil Friday Jul 17 in Berlin: [Jul 17 00:00 CEST, Jul 18 00:00 CEST) = [2026-07-16T22:00Z, 2026-07-17T22:00Z) — bounds land at 22:00Z, not midnight UTC. Double trap: PM-612 (2026-07-16T22:15Z) is Friday 00:15 CEST — inside — while PM-618 (2026-07-17T22:30Z) is Saturday 00:30 CEST — outside — yet naive UTC-day bounds [Jul 17 00Z, Jul 18 00Z) select exactly the wrong one of the pair. PM-615 (Friday noon local) is interior; PM-604 is due today (Thu). Correct: 2 tickets, PM-612 and PM-615.

scenarios.title: issue-last-updated-plain

checks.note: 2:22pm EDT July 17 — UTC and local agree on the day

scenarios.rationale: Trap-free baseline, pure time→NL: get_issue(PM-207) returns updated_utc = 2026-07-17T18:22:00Z, which is FRIDAY July 17 2026, 2:22pm EDT — the UTC and New York calendar days coincide, so there is no rejection trap; the scenario simply checks that the day (July 17 / Friday) is reported. A search_issues mock carrying the same row is provided in case the agent searches instead of looking up by ID.

scenarios.title: kolkata-due-this-weekend

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: Anchored on Thursday Jul 9, nl2time's PRIMARY resolution is the already-past Jul 4-5 weekend ([2026-07-03T18:30Z .. 2026-07-05T18:30Z), the current Sunday-start week's Sat-Sun); the upcoming Sat Jul 11-Sun Jul 12 weekend — the only sensible reading of a due-date question — appears only in its alternatives. nl2time issue-worthy.

checks.note: PM-702 (Sat 1:30am IST), PM-705 (Sat 10am), PM-709 (Sun 6pm); PM-713 is Monday 00:15 IST

scenarios.rationale: Now = THURSDAY Jul 9 2026, 7:05pm IST (Asia/Kolkata, UTC+5:30 — non-integer-hour offset). This weekend = the upcoming Sat Jul 11 + Sun Jul 12: [Sat Jul 11 00:00 IST, Mon Jul 13 00:00 IST) = [2026-07-10T18:30Z, 2026-07-12T18:30Z) — bounds land at :30 past the UTC hour. Traps: PM-702 (2026-07-10T20:00Z) is Saturday 1:30am IST — inside — but a naive UTC weekend [Jul 11 00Z, Jul 13 00Z) drops it; PM-713 (2026-07-12T18:45Z) is Monday 00:15 IST — outside — but the naive UTC window keeps it. PM-705 (Sat 10:00am IST) and PM-709 (Sun 6:00pm IST) are interior; PM-698 is due today (Thu). Count = 3.

scenarios.title: updated-three-days-ago
scenarios.user: Show me what was updated three days ago.

checks.note: PM-801 and PM-806 on Tue Jul 21; PM-797 is Monday, PM-810 Wednesday

scenarios.rationale: Trap-free baseline. Now = FRIDAY Jul 24 2026, 9:00am EDT. 'Three days ago' = the civil day Tuesday Jul 21 in New York: [Jul 21 00:00 ET, Jul 22 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-21T04:00Z, 2026-07-22T04:00Z), matching the bridge exactly. In range: PM-801 (Tue 10:30am EDT) and PM-806 (Tue 4:10pm EDT) — count 2. PM-797 (Mon Jul 20, 2:00pm EDT) and PM-810 (Wed Jul 22, 11:00am EDT) sit safely on neighboring days with no cross-midnight ambiguity — UTC and local days agree for every row.
